doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

chapter: Life and work in New York
title: Marriage to actor Joe Grifasi and artists' work cycles
summary: Both are performers who understand travel and uneven work.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And your husband is Joe Grafasi? Did I pronounce that right?
And being that he’s an actor, both of you are in professions that can be a little perilous at times I would think.
Well we’re both performers. We understand what that means. The lifestyle and the travel and what it means to really prepare yourself for performance. We understand that about each other.
Without getting too personal, has there ever been a time where you’ve both had a stretch of a month or so where the work seems to be down?
Your work flow. I imagine being that you’re both basically self employed, it’s kind of up and down.
Does it ever happen where you’re both like down?

Of course, sure. It’s just in the natural flow of events. But you know you have faith. If you’ve been doing it long enough eventually something’s going to happen. But sure there’s been all kinds of matches, you know I’m up, he’s down; he’s up, I’m down; we’re both up; we’re both down. All possibilities exist in the life of artists.
